findings.reason: the worker would place the lift lookup at whichever of the two named seams it reads first, and if it follows the negative control into `policy()` the reset-anchored expiry it must implement there is impossible to evaluate, so the node's declared control does not prove the guard fires.
findings.text: the negative control "deletes the lift lookup from `pace.policy` alone", but §10 line 1924 says the lift is applied "given the group, the reading and the time" and — as the cited code shows — `pace.policy(config)` (reckon/crew/pace.py:128) takes only `config` and reads nothing but `drain_lead_hours` and `pace_multiple`; it has no group, no reading and no clock, so it cannot evaluate a lift's reset/`max_hours`/`at` end conditions, and the control as written can never redden

findings.reason: the section names only the pace seam as the single application point, so a worker implementing it would raise the multiple and leave the reserve block untouched, failing the section's own 100%-ceiling done-when.
findings.text: "A lift raises the pace multiple and releases the reserves" and the done-when (line 1950) asserts the implementation ceiling "reads 100% with all three reserves at zero", but the reserves are not computed through `pace.allowance_for_group`; `reckon/crew/reserve.py` `reserve_pct`/`role_ceiling_pct` read the raw budget block, reached by `reserve_admit_windows((config or {}).get("budget") or {}, …)` at reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:308, a path the "one seam … none computes its own" paragraph does not name
